items.name: Most sources block simple automated reading
items.what: Every government and news site we tested refused our basic page reader; we read them through a scraping service with a tight rate limit, which slows each check.

items.name: New York Times
items.what: Could not be read automatically at all. Its stories appear here only when other outlets or records confirm them.

items.name: AP and Reuters
items.what: No working news feeds. AP is not in the Wire; Reuters is followed through a news search that catches only some stories.

items.name: Paywalls
items.what: Bloomberg, the Wall Street Journal, The Information, RTO Insider, Law360 and E&E News show headlines only. We use them as leads and confirm facts elsewhere.

items.name: Federal contract awards
items.what: The USAspending search cannot be queried with our tools, so contracts are found through agency announcements and news, often later.

items.name: FERC and state utility commissions
items.what: FERC has no news feed and its document library is a search form; several state commissions (Virginia, Pennsylvania, Georgia) do not list news in a readable way. Decisions can reach us a day or more late.

items.name: County and city meetings
items.what: Local rezoning votes, tax abatements and nondisclosure agreements have no central source. We depend on local news and Data Center Watch, so smaller places are under-covered.

items.name: New lawsuits
items.what: We read court opinions, not new filings in federal dockets (PACER). New cases appear when agencies or outlets report them.

items.name: Money in politics lags by design
items.what: Lobbying and campaign-finance totals appear only when quarterly filings are due, weeks or months after the money was spent.

items.name: The Wire is unverified and not instant
items.what: GitHub runs the headline collector every 5 to 15 minutes, and news searches include some off-topic items. Nothing in the Wire has been checked.
